projects.name: MoodMuse
description: A journaling web app that turns daily mood check-ins into generative canvas art and a calm weekly recap. I built it after noticing most mood trackers felt like spreadsheets — people would log a number, close the tab, and never look back.

Entries are stored as structured notes rather than a single score. A small Node API scores language for valence, then the frontend maps that into color, motion, and density so each week produces a unique piece of art. Insights are written in plain language ("you slept better on days you went outside") instead of charts nobody reads.
highlights: 1.2k registered users in the first semester, with about 40% returning the following week.
Canvas renderer keeps a 60fps animation on mid-range laptops by batching draws and pausing off-screen tabs.
Weekly email digest is optional and can be turned off in one tap — no dark patterns.

projects.name: OrbitDesk
description: A keyboard-first task manager for people who bounce off most to-do apps. Everything lives behind a command palette: capture a task, snooze it, or jump to a project without touching the mouse.

The app is offline-first. Tasks live in IndexedDB and a service worker keeps a local copy of the UI, so it still works on a train with no signal. When the network returns, a last-write-wins sync with conflict notes keeps two devices from silently dropping work.
highlights: Command palette handles create, search, reschedule, and tag in under 200ms on a cold start.
Sync recovers after going offline for a weekend; conflicts surface as a short note instead of a merge UI.
Shipped without accounts for the first month so classmates could try it from a static host.

projects.name: SnackTrack
description: A campus food-truck tracker with live locations, today's menus, and a rough crowd meter so you do not walk across quad for a truck that already left. Built with two friends for Hack the Aurora 2024.

Vendors drop a pin from a phone and update a short menu; students see trucks on a Leaflet map with filters for cuisine and dietary tags. Crowd level is a three-step estimate from check-ins in the last 20 minutes, not a fake heatmap.
highlights: Won Best Campus Hack; student government asked us to keep it running through finals week.
Map stays usable on a 4G phone: tiles are cached and the live layer is a handful of GeoJSON points.
Vendors can post a menu in under a minute without creating a separate dashboard account.
